verdict.rationale: Unstructured's own docs describe partitioning into document elements with metadata in a consistent JSON format. A chunking step then regroups those elements to fit embedding-model limits, with by-title, by-page and by-similarity strategies, and jobs can embed the chunks into AI-ready JSON with vector embeddings. That covers semantic boundaries, metadata and embedding-ready segments. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of chunk quality, and detail on which metadata fields survive chunking.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, output comes pre-chunked for RAG — semantic boundaries, metadata, embedding-ready segments — not a wall of text

citations.quote: After partitioning, _chunking_ rearranges the resulting document elements into manageable “chunks” to stay within the limits of an embedding model and to improve retrieval precision.
You can further control this behavior with by title, by page, and by similarity chunking strategies.

_Partitioning_ converts content from unstructured files and semi-structured data records into structured [document elements and metadata](/concepts/document-elements) in a predefined, consistent, expressive, and contextualized JSON format.
Create a job to partition, chunk, and embed local files into AI-ready JSON with vector embeddings for semantic search.
output the results as partitioned, enriched, chunked, and embedded data, ready for your immediate use.
